056cee89-1826-4ee3-b06c-53d5880ed132.heading: Car speeds up from 30 to 70 km/h in 6 minutes

beats.say: With constant acceleration the speed rises steadily from 30 to 70 kilometres per hour.
So the average speed is 30 plus 70, over 2: 50 kilometres per hour.
The time is 6 minutes, which is 6 over 60, or 0.10 hours.
Distance is average speed times time: 50 times 0.10 is 5.0 kilometres.

1ce2afbb-71f0-4744-91a9-94026334af89.heading: Distance from 0 to 6 s under the graph

beats.say: Distance is the area under the speed-time graph.
From 0 to 2 seconds it is a triangle: a half, times 2, times 10, is 10 metres.
From 2 to 6 seconds it is a rectangle: 4 times 10 is 40 metres.
Add them: 10 plus 40 is 50 metres.

2609a9a3-5866-4989-9d99-08bfaefae4a7.heading: Free fall for 5.0 s — how tall is the building?

beats.say: In free fall the speed-time graph is a straight line from rest.
Its gradient is the acceleration, 10 metres per second squared.
After 5.0 seconds the speed is 10 times 5.0, which is 50 metres per second.
The height is the area under the graph: a half, times 50, times 5.0, is 125 metres.
The gradient of a distance-time graph is the speed.
Here it is 2 metres in 1 second: 2.0 metres per second.
The line is straight, so the speed is constant. A distance graph shows no direction, and the acceleration is 0.
The distance-time graph is a straight line, so the speed is constant and the acceleration is 0.
The speed is the gradient: 50 minus 10, over 5, is 8 metres per second.
The distance travelled is 50 minus 10, which is 40 metres.

4271ed7b-5a44-4bdb-8aa1-2ff9c360993a.heading: Which statement about the car is incorrect?

beats.say: The speed rises by 3 metres per second every second, so the speed-time graph is a straight line from the origin.
So the acceleration is uniform at 3 metres per second squared.
In 2 seconds the average speed is 0 plus 6, over 2, which is 3 metres per second.
So the distance is 3 times 2, which is 6 metres, not 12 metres. Statement B is the incorrect one.
The spacecraft rises while its velocity is positive.
It reaches its highest point when the velocity is 0, at 20 hours.
The height is the area of the triangle: a half, times 20, times 5000, is 50000 kilometres.

473c3a4c-45f8-45cc-9579-8a5c5590f23c.heading: Average acceleration from 2.0 s to 3.0 s

beats.say: Here is the athlete's speed from the table, second by second.
Average acceleration is the change in speed divided by the time.
5.7 minus 4.1 is 1.6, over 1.0 second: 1.6 metres per second squared.
First the main road: 8.0 kilometres in 10 minutes.
Then the side road: 2.0 kilometres in 5.0 minutes.
Total distance: 8.0 plus 2.0 is 10 kilometres, in 15 minutes.
15 minutes is 0.25 hours.
Average speed is total distance over total time: 10 over 0.25 is 40 kilometres per hour.
The toy car speeds up, then moves at a steady 8.0 metres per second.
In the constant-deceleration section the speed falls steadily from 8.0 metres per second to 0.
So the average speed is 8.0 plus 0, over 2, which is 4.0 metres per second.

70792cb2-dedc-4fb8-ab0e-b232779a94f7.answerText: \text{The car accelerates at a constant rate}
70792cb2-dedc-4fb8-ab0e-b232779a94f7.heading: Speed-time graph: 0 to 14 m/s in 24 s

beats.say: The graph is a straight sloping line, so the acceleration is constant.
Its gradient is 14 over 24, about 0.58 metres per second squared.
The distance is the area under the graph: a half, times 24, times 14, is 168 metres, not 336. So C is wrong.
At 24 seconds the speed is 14 metres per second, so B is wrong. The speed changes, so D is wrong.

8ac3d5df-0614-4ed7-b2b4-ba30a517e87f.heading: Average speed over 100 km, with a rest

beats.say: First 40 kilometres in 45 minutes.
Then a rest of 15 minutes.
Then the last 60 kilometres in 1 hour, which is 60 minutes.
Total time: 45 plus 15 plus 60 is 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.
Average speed is total distance over total time: 100 kilometres over 2 hours is 50 kilometres per hour.

line.why: total distance ÷ total time, rest included

8e4ffc70-8d02-40b5-8e1f-a11e261f6ce7.heading: Dropped from 125 m: how long to fall?

beats.say: The speed-time graph rises in a straight line from rest.
Its gradient is the acceleration, 10 metres per second squared.
It rises to 50 metres per second in 5 seconds.
The displacement is the area: a half, times 5, times 50, is 125 metres, the height of the building. So the time is 5 seconds.

959655b4-46ea-4a3c-8a87-ec0080d33fee.heading: 2000 m race: speed up for 10 s, then steady

beats.say: From rest he accelerates at 10.0 metres per second squared for 10 seconds.
After 10 seconds his speed is 10 times 10, which is 100 metres per second.
He has covered a half, times 10, times 10 squared, which is 500 metres.
The remaining 1500 metres at 100 metres per second takes 15 seconds.
The whole race takes 10 plus 15, which is 25 seconds.

96f1241a-016a-41a0-b551-ebb14906d6ce.heading: Speed up to 40 m/s, then steady to 1.0 km

beats.say: From rest he accelerates at 2.0 metres per second squared up to 40 metres per second.
That takes 40 over 2.0, which is 20 seconds.
In that time he covers a half, times 2.0, times 20 squared, which is 400 metres.
The last 600 metres at 40 metres per second takes 15 seconds.
Total time: 20 plus 15 is 35 seconds.

9f9425b0-75e5-4eeb-8c1d-d41470b467bb.heading: Truck: how far between 0 and 10 s?

beats.say: The speed rises steadily from 0 to 50 metres per second in 10 seconds.
Distance is the area under the speed-time graph, a triangle: a half, times 10, times 50, is 250 metres.
500 metres is base times height: it forgets the half for a triangle.
The graph is a straight line from the origin to 400 seconds and 20 metres per second.
So the area under it is a triangle: a half, times 400, times 20, is 4000 metres.

aa12e474-ad17-40ea-aa54-4ea81dd4e8c6.heading: Decelerating car — how much longer to stop?

beats.say: The car slows steadily from 6.0 metres per second to v over 2.0 seconds.
It covers 10 metres: average velocity times time, a half of 6.0 plus v, times 2.0.
So v is 4.0 metres per second.
The deceleration is the drop in speed over the time: 6.0 minus 4.0, over 2.0, is 1.0 metres per second squared.
At the same rate, from 4.0 metres per second it needs 4.0 over 1.0, which is 4.0 more seconds.
First stage: 90 metres in 30 seconds.
Second stage: a further 80 metres in another 20 seconds.
Average speed is total distance over total time.
That is 170 over 50, which is 3.40 metres per second.

acc03c47-b2ab-4d59-9409-7c13bfcc4170.heading: Stone dropped for 5.0 s — speed at the water

beats.say: Dropped, so it starts from rest: the speed-time line starts at 0.
With no air resistance, the acceleration is g, 10 metres per second squared.
v equals u plus a t: 0 plus 10 times 5.0, which is 50 metres per second.

b8b498ac-60b7-4232-8d64-6111330a2277.heading: Cyclist stops in 3.0 m from 5.0 m/s

beats.say: The speed falls steadily from 5.0 metres per second to 0.
The distance, 3.0 metres, is the area under the speed-time graph: a half, times 5, times t.
So t is 1.2 seconds.
Here is the speed-time graph of the car.
The flat part is the constant speed: 10 metres per second, from 20 seconds to 40 seconds.
Distance is speed times time, the area under the flat part: 10 times 20 is 200 metres.

c17bd487-9485-417e-993c-d9f299ff1603.heading: Thrown down at 5 m/s, 20 m/s after 2 s

beats.say: The speed rises from 5 metres per second to 20 metres per second in 2 seconds.
Acceleration is the change in speed over the time: 20 minus 5, over 2, is 7.5 metres per second squared.
The speed rises from 0 to 12 metres per second in 3 seconds.
Distance is the area under the graph, a triangle: a half, times 3, times 12, is 18 metres.

d0b2f427-bc79-4d81-a2fd-e9531144581b.heading: Average speed: main road then side road

beats.say: The main road: 100 kilometres in 60 minutes.
Then the side road: 20 kilometres in 30 minutes.
Total distance: 100 plus 20 is 120 kilometres.
Total time: 60 plus 30 is 90 minutes, which is 1.5 hours.
Average speed: 120 over 1.5 is 80 kilometres per hour.

d106f2bc-bf22-44eb-84f7-be883bf9d67e.heading: Train at t = 15.0 s — which way, faster or slower?

beats.say: North at a constant 20 metres per second until t equals 5.0 seconds.
Then the acceleration is minus 1.5 metres per second squared.
It acts for 15.0 minus 5.0, which is 10.0 seconds.
v equals 20 plus minus 1.5 times 10.0, which is 5 metres per second.
The velocity is still positive, so the train is still going north, but slowing down.

d3935321-d8eb-4842-8e30-739940279a0f.heading: Helicopter: 50 m/s, then 2 m/s² for 10 s

beats.say: The helicopter starts at 50 metres per second.
It speeds up uniformly at 2 metres per second squared for 10 seconds.
v equals u plus a t: 50 plus 2 times 10, which is 70 metres per second.

d7b3e402-cc54-4853-b18c-99088c0d653a.heading: Rocket from 500 to 1500 m/s in 5.0 s

beats.say: The speed rises uniformly from 500 to 1500 metres per second in 5.0 seconds.
Uniform acceleration, so the average speed is halfway: 500 plus 1500, over 2, is 1000 metres per second.
Distance is the average speed times the time: 1000 times 5.0 is 5000 metres.

db9e10d7-54b7-4e13-813d-519e5e262fa6.heading: Bus at t = 15.0 s — which way, faster or slower?

beats.say: North at 25 metres per second until t equals 5.0 seconds.
Then the acceleration is minus 2.0 metres per second squared, for 10 seconds up to t equals 15.
v equals 25 plus minus 2.0 times 10, which is plus 5 metres per second.
Still positive, so the bus is still going north, but slowing down.

dd9163d3-fb2c-4b59-8711-86c9683da174.heading: Toy cart — average speed over 12 s

beats.say: The cart's distance-time graph runs from 0 to 12 seconds.
It starts at d equals 2 metres, not 0.
It ends at 9 metres, so it travels 9 minus 2, which is 7 metres.
The total time is 12 seconds.
Average speed: 7 over 12 is 0.583, about 0.58 metres per second.

e3e4dccc-0358-44b6-b81c-0dd684ef7397.heading: Car from 40 to 80 km/h in 3 minutes

beats.say: The speed rises steadily from 40 to 80 kilometres per hour in 3 minutes.
Constant acceleration, so the average speed is 40 plus 80, over 2: 60 kilometres per hour.
3 minutes is 3 over 60 of an hour. Distance: 60 times 3 over 60 is 3.0 kilometres.

e4084ee0-1baf-46b6-ac1b-011c4d4db8d1.heading: Race car stops in 1.7 s at 20 m/s²

beats.say: The car slows at 20 metres per second squared and stops after 1.7 seconds.
So its initial speed is a times t: 20 times 1.7, which is 34 metres per second.
Then s equals u squared over 2a: 34 squared over 2 times 20, about 29 metres.

eb7d86df-f811-4b3d-a199-35eb9ff1b962.heading: Round trip: average speed in m/s

beats.say: Out: 120 kilometres in 100 minutes.
Back: another 120 kilometres in 1 hour, 60 minutes.
Total distance: 120 plus 120 is 240 kilometres, which is 240 000 metres.
Total time: 100 plus 60 is 160 minutes, which is 9600 seconds.
Average speed: 240 000 over 9600 is 25 metres per second.
The car starts at 2.0 metres per second.
It accelerates at 0.20 metres per second squared.
For 2.5 minutes, which is 2.5 times 60, 150 seconds.
v equals u plus a t: 2.0 plus 0.20 times 150.
That is 2.0 plus 30, which is 32 metres per second.

f2140fae-b68a-45c4-a241-d2bd6a05b2aa.heading: From rest to 10 m/s in 10 s

beats.say: From rest, the speed rises uniformly to 10 metres per second in 10 seconds.
Acceleration is the change in speed over the time: 10 minus 0, over 10, is 1 metre per second squared.

f9796e34-cb78-4e67-8d99-51667b97b731.heading: Car stopping in sand at 2.5 m/s²

beats.say: The car enters the sand at 10 metres per second and slows uniformly to 0.
The deceleration is 2.5 metres per second squared.
a equals v minus u over t, so t is 0 minus 10, over minus 2.5: 4.0 seconds.
The object speeds up to 20 metres per second in 20 seconds, then holds that speed to 50 seconds.
Distance in the first 20 seconds is the triangle: a half, times 20, times 20, is 200 metres.
In the last 30 seconds, the rectangle: 20 times 30 is 600 metres.
Total distance: 200 plus 600 is 800 metres.
Average speed is total distance over total time: 800 over 50 is 16 metres per second.
